chainTitle: What it cites, and who cites it
chainIntro: The plan names two instruments, and neither is a Chinese government document. The Pact for the Future (《未来契约》) and the Global Digital Compact (《全球数字契约》) were adopted by the UN General Assembly at the Summit of the Future in September 2024, the Compact as an annex to the Pact. The corpus holds neither, so both are marked as absent references in the text.

The plan cites no domestic law, regulation or prior Chinese policy by name. Its verbs are 呼吁, 鼓励, 支持 and 倡导 (call on, encourage, support, advocate), addressed to governments, international organisations, firms, research bodies, civil-society organisations and individuals alike. The one 应 (should) is in point 9, and it binds public sectors.

Point 2 borrows a domestic slogan, “人工智能+” (AI+), in quotation marks and without a citation. The State Council’s own instrument of that name, 《国务院关于深入实施“人工智能+”行动的意见》, is dated 21 August and was published 26 August 2025 (corpus id 12650908, gov), a month after this plan. The international text used the label before the domestic one existed.
citedByIntro: Every row below is a document in the corpus whose citation edge resolves to the plan. Level and genre come from the per-document identity layer, not from the publishing site, so a provincial portal reposting a Xinhua readout counts as a sub-national readout, not as a central one.
Read the genre column before the level column. A document that cites the plan is not thereby implementing it.
